newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's SBI index up two pct at five-month high.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's SBI index up two pct at five-month high.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index extended its winning streak for the fourth session on Wednesday, ending at its highest level in five months -- and traders said more gains could be expected.

"I think the index could easily exceed its all-time high (1,655.4) by the end of summer as some shares that have a big impact on movements in the index still have plenty of room on the upside," said Mili Kus of Eastbrokers.
The SBI rose 32.15 points or 2.15 percent to 1,524.45.

"It looks like it will be easy to exceed the psychological limit of 2,000 points in a bit more than a month, unless the central bank plays some more with rules for foreign investors," one broker said.
Overall 15 shares rose, five fell and one was flat, while seven were untraded. Turnover eased to 529.2 million tolars from 616.9 million.
Petrol trader Petrol was the most active share, jumping 5.65 percent or 1,270 tolars to 23,750 tolars on volume of 11,899 shares for total turnover of 274.5 million tolars.

"When Petrol was listed there were no foreign investors present here and now they are buying so much to catch what they missed then. This could push Petrol to about 25,000 by the end of summer," Kus said.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, jumping 10 percent to 9,680 tolars on volume of only 10 shares.
Bank UBK led decliners, tumbling 10 percent to 6,300 tolars on volume of 23 shares.
